title: Using an AED
tldr: For an unresponsive person who is not breathing normally, call emergency services and begin CPR. Turn on the AED as soon as it arrives and follow its voice and picture prompts. Do not touch the person during rhythm analysis or a shock.
steps: Continue CPR while another helper prepares the AED if possible.
Dry a wet chest and place pads according to the AED diagrams.
Make sure no one touches the person during analysis or shock delivery.
Immediately follow the device instructions to continue compressions.
next: Keep the AED connected until responders take over. Learn the location of nearby devices and obtain training.
watch: For a child or infant, use the appropriate pediatric pads or setting when available and follow the device and dispatcher instructions.
review_status: source-linked editorial review; not independent expert certification
without_help: If nobody can bring an AED, continue CPR rather than leaving the person to search alone. If another person is present, ask them to locate the nearest accessible AED while you continue compressions. Follow the device prompts when it arrives.
household: Give someone the specific task of calling or locating care while another person provides first aid. Keep the patient warm or cool as the condition requires and record what happened and when. Do not put yourself into the same hazard or assume an ambulance has been dispatched until confirmed.
pack_now: Keep essential medicines, drinking water, a battery light, shoes, phone power and a written contact card within reach. Adapt the load to the hazard and the people with you; do not delay escape to collect equipment.
